answer_text:
Let

\[
f(z)=\frac{1}{(z^2+1)^3}=\frac{1}{(z-i)^3(z+i)^3}.
\]

We integrate over the upper semicircular contour of radius \(R\) centered at the origin and let \(R\to\infty\). The only pole inside the contour is at \(z=i\), and it is a pole of order \(3\).

For \(|z|=R\),

\[
|f(z)|\le \frac{1}{(R^2-1)^3},
\]

so the integral over the semicircle has magnitude at most

\[
\frac{\pi R}{(R^2-1)^3}\to 0 \qquad (R\to\infty).
\]

Thus

\[
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\frac{dx}{(x^2+1)^3}
=
2\pi i\,\operatorname{Res}_{z=i} f(z).
\]

Now compute the residue at the third-order pole \(z=i\):

\[
\operatorname{Res}_{z=i} f(z)
=
\frac{1}{2!}
\left.
\frac{d^2}{dz^2}\left((z-i)^3 f(z)\right)
\right|_{z=i}.
\]

But

\[
(z-i)^3 f(z)=\frac{1}{(z+i)^3}.
\]

So let

\[
g(z)=\frac{1}{(z+i)^3}=(z+i)^{-3}.
\]

Then

\[
g'(z)=-3(z+i)^{-4},
\]

and

\[
g''(z)=12(z+i)^{-5}.
\]

Evaluate at \(z=i\):

\[
g''(i)=12(2i)^{-5}.
\]

Since

\[
(2i)^5=32i^5=32i,
\]

we get

\[
g''(i)=\frac{12}{32i}=\frac{3}{8i}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\operatorname{Res}_{z=i} f(z)
=
\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{3}{8i}
=
\frac{3}{16i}.
\]

Hence

\[
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\frac{dx}{(x^2+1)^3}
=
2\pi i\cdot \frac{3}{16i}
=
\frac{3\pi}{8}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{3\pi}{8}}
\]
